newsitem.title: USA: CFTC opposes House bill to revise US futures law.
newsitem.headline: CFTC opposes House bill to revise US futures law.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission opposes a House bill to revise the basic U.S. futures-trading law, chairman Brooksley Born told a House Agriculture subcommittee Tuesday.
Born listed five objections to the bill sponsored by subcommittee chairman Tom Ewing, R-Ill. In three of them, she said the bill would remove important safeguards to assure fair trading.
"The provisions relating to professional markets and the Treasury amendment would result in pervasive deregulation of U.S. futures and option markets," Born said.

Elimination of "even the most basic regulatory protections," she said, would open the door to a U.S. version of misdeeds such as the Barings Bank collapse from improper trading on the Singapore exchange.

Born also objected to exemption from federal oversight of all over-the-counter transactions among sophisticated traders, an onerouse cost-benefit analysis for most CFTC actions, repeal of enhanced audit trail rules and absurdly short time periods for the CFTC to act before a new contract or new exchange rules could automatically take effect.

The Ewing bill would allow a professionals-only market to be created for all futures contracts and options trading, Born said. The result, she said, would be "elimilnation of virtually all regulation of our exchanges."

"The exchanges estimate that approximately 90 percent of the volume of trading on their markets is currently on behalf of persons who would be eligible to trade in an unregulated environment under this legislation," Born said.
